summary: After leaving school, about half of a young person's closest friends are still close eighteen months later, and the new friends crowd the old ones out.
realLife: A small study followed 25 students for 18 months after leaving school and found about half of inner-circle friends remained, with a drop in closeness tied to adding many new friends and attending university.
sources: PubMed Central, longitudinal study of friendships after leaving school: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4626528
inGame: friend ties' closeness after the school record ends; new friend ties formed at a new job or place.

turns.summary: The old friends keep up through weekly plans.
Calls become rare as new friends fill the time.
A friend reaches out years later and they reconnect.
